correctness.rationale: For a palindrome P(a,b,c), the full eight-coordinate scattered three-deck equals (binom(N,3),H,2N(N-1)-2H,N+t,H,4N-2t,N+t,4) with t=4a+b and H=N^2+2Na-Nt-N+10a^2-6at+t^2. Equality reduces to fixed (N,t,H); the quadratic difference factorization (a-a′)(10(a+a′)+2N-6t)=0 proves at most two in-class sources. The unique nontrivial solution is integral iff the oriented difference b-c=5d with d>0, yielding P(a,c+5d,c) and P(a+d,c+d,c+6d) and proving unique orientation. Counting N=2a+3c+10d gives the generating function and asymptotic 2/15. Actual standalone verifier independently checked 45,526 gap instances through N=100, 385 direct triple-position decks through N=18, all complete inverse fibers through N=100, and coefficients to N=500. These finite tests are explicitly non-exhaustive for the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The full primary text of Angal et al. (arxiv:2610.41110v1, Section 3.1, Remark 3.2) already exhibits the first length-14 ambiguous palindrome pair and proves other reconstruction thresholds, so that pair is credited as prior. Its cited statements do not classify the entire fixed-weight palindromic three-deck relation, count all inverse fibers at every length or derive the two-fifteenths limit. The unrestricted k-deck enumeration article covers tables/global bounds, not these constrained inverse fibers. Indexed near neighbors cover unrestricted weight four, weight three, bounded run counts or other palindrome questions; their statements do not imply this exact all-length classification. value.rationale: A natural symmetry-constrained class at binary weight four exhibits strict bounded decoding-list size two, despite unbounded three-deck ambiguity for unrestricted four-one words. The all-parameter involution certifies exact zero-error distinguishability, the rational series counts every collision at all lengths, and the 2/15 limit quantifies asymptotic ambiguity under uniform fixed-content symmetric sampling. These are structural and information-theoretic results, not a single small-case recomputation.
